editorial:
Imagine being stuck between a rock and a hard place while riding a train toward a dream that might never happen. You follow Sayra, a young girl who just wants a safe life, and a gang member named Mano who is trying to escape a violent world. The movie puts you right in the middle of the dangerous journey from Central America to the US. It feels very real and gritty, almost like you are sitting right there on the roof of the train with them. The tension is high from the start, and you really feel for these characters as they try to survive people who want to hurt them.

The acting is great because it feels natural and not like a polished Hollywood movie. The action is sudden and scary, which keeps you on the edge of your seat. One downside is that it can be quite sad and stressful, so it is not exactly a lighthearted popcorn flick. If you love stories about survival and human courage, you need to see this.
endingExplained: At the end, Mano helps Sayra and her father get away safely, showing he has changed his ways. However, his old gang catches up to him. In a final confrontation, Mano is killed by the gang members he tried to leave behind. He dies so that Sayra can have the chance at a better life. The movie ends with Sayra finally reaching the United States, though she carries the weight of the sacrifice made for her.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves intense survival stories and emotional dramas.
